 Millions of ladders sold at Costco, Lowe's recalled after reports of serious injuries 
 The recall was issued after Little Giant received 25 reports of the ladders retracting, including 19 that stated people were injured. 
 By Izzy Stroobandt • 
 Published November 7, 2026 • 
 Updated on November 7, 2026 at 3:51 pm 
 BOOKMARKER 
 You’re watching the NBC 5 Chicago News streaming channel, which plays local Chicago news 24 hours a day, seven days a week. You can find the “NBC 5 Chicago News” streaming channel on your phone or computer, and on Peacock, Samsung, Roku, Xumo or on our app, so you can watch our local news on your schedule.
 Millions of ladders sold at Costco, Lowe's and other popular retailers were recalled because of a fall risk that left several people seriously injured, according to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission.
 The recall , that was issued on Thursday, applies to roughly 3.6 million Little Giant ladders with rapid locks, according to the recall alert. The models that are subject to the recall are the Adjustable Fortress 2.0, Conquest 2.0, Dark Horse 2.0, Epic, King Kombo XT, Leveler, MegaLite, MegaLite+, Multi, Quantum and Vector with orange rectangular “QC” sticker on the rail above one of the rapid locks.

 "The ladders can suddenly retract if the Rapid Locks are not fully engaged, posing a fall hazard to consumers," the recall alert states. 
 The recall was issued after Little Giant received 25 reports of the ladders retracting, including 19 that stated people were injured. Three people reported head injuries, such as traumatic brain injury, skull fracture, concussion, vision loss, hearing loss and cognitive impairment, and 16 reports of join or bone fracture, lacerations and bruising were made. 
 Little Giant also received 39 reports that the rapid locks did not work properly. 
 The ladders were sold at Lowe’s, Costco and other stores nationwide and online at Lowes.com, Amazon.com, Costco.com, LittleGiantLadders.com and other websites starting in December 2015 through October 2026. 
 One of the ladder models included in the recall. 
 Anyone with a ladder included in the recall is advised to stop using it "immediately" until they review the information here and contact Little Giant for a repair kit that comes with warning labels and instructions, according to the recall alert.

 "Consumers who follow the provided instructions and have a Rapid Lock that does not function properly after the application of lubrication should contact Little Giant for evaluation. If a lock does not function properly after this evaluation, the company will offer the choice of a replacement ladder of the same or equivalent model or a refund ranging from a depreciated value determined by date of purchase up to full purchase price for ladders purchased within the past 12 months," the recall alert says.
